title: Getting Started with MultiStateTMLE
text: first step model hazard event. fit_initial() takes one formula per event, event left covariates hazard right. Using another event’s name covariate gives number events far, death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness lets illness change death hazard: default hazard Cox model, death hazard \begin{aligned}     \lambda_{\text{death}}(t) = \lambda_0(t) \exp\big(      & \beta_1 \, \text{biomarker} + \beta_2 \, \text{treatment} \\      & + \beta_3 \, \text{illness}(t) \big),   \end{aligned} \text{illness}(t) 1 patient fallen ill. tau = 1 time horizon: everything concerns happens time 1. Every event data needs model, censoring included. plain formula short hazard_model(formula), also takes limit, events patient can (one illness), at_risk, condition ~ illness == 0 patients risk.
code: models <- list(   hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),   death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,   censoring ~ biomarker ) fit <- fit_initial(illness_death, models = models, tau = 1) fit #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE

title: Getting Started with MultiStateTMLE
text: Often question risks directly: drug prevented 20% illnesses? calibrate() finds factor \alpha risk illness reaches given value, estimates risk death : first table gives calibrated \alpha risk illness \theta reaches, 80% observed 0.369. second gives risk death . target risk illness can given three ways: level(theta): risk theta. absolute_change(delta): risk delta plus observed value. relative_change(rho): risk rho times observed value. \alpha estimated, standard error se accounts uncertainty. se_crude standard error \alpha known. years_lost() gives expected years life lost tau instead risk, can used wherever risk() can:
code: calibrated <- tmle_estimate(   fit,   risk(death),   calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) ) calibrated #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se     lower     upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:    alpha 0.7443751 0.01232345 0.7202216 0.7685287 #> 2:    theta 0.2950367 0.02790535 0.2403432 0.3497301 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se    lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.3127176 0.03330144 0.247448 0.3779872 0.03338458 coef(tmle_estimate(   fit,   years_lost(death),   calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) )) #>     death  #> 0.1596098

text: far treatment covariate. Suppose instead want effect death, much treated patients fall ill less often. calibrated intervention answers : give patients treatment, calibrate risk illness placebo. splits total effect two contrasts: mediated: treatment versus calibrated intervention, part goes illness, calibrated: calibrated intervention versus placebo, rest. treatment_model tells fit_initial() treatment assigned, estimates can made everyone treated everyone placebo: sets everyone’s treatment, reference_a = 0 calibrates risk illness placebo: give treated patients risk illness placebo, illness hazard must multiplied 2.7. calibrated_contrasts() combines three fits: Treatment lowers risk death 18 percentage points, 6 go illness. true_model , simevent gives true contrasts : simulate arm without censoring, calibrated arm search factor illness hazard matches risk illness placebo: Every interval covers truth. 200 patients contrasts estimated less precisely risks, since compares two arms 100.
code: trial_fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = models,   tau = 1,   treatment_model = treatment ~ biomarker ) treated <- tmle_estimate(trial_fit, risk(death), a = 1) placebo <- tmle_estimate(trial_fit, risk(death), a = 0) treated_calibrated <- tmle_estimate(   trial_fit,   risk(death),   calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(1), reference_a = 0),   a = 1 ) treated_calibrated #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(1), reference_a = 0), with a = 1 #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se     lower    upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>    <num> #> 1:    alpha 2.6814303 0.72116544 1.2679720 4.094889 #> 2:    theta 0.4974118 0.05135867 0.3967507 0.598073 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se    lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.3112979 0.06357508 0.186693 0.4359028 0.06411261 contrasts <- calibrated_contrasts(treated, placebo, treated_calibrated) contrasts #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast    estimate         se      lower         upper #>    <char>     <char>       <num>      <num>      <num>         <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.18273318 0.06913193 -0.3182293 -0.0472370913 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.06387838 0.03275458 -0.1280762  0.0003194037 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.11885480 0.08063644 -0.2768993  0.0391897229 placebo_risks <- true_risks(list(treatment = 0)) treatment_risks <- true_risks(list(treatment = 1)) true_alpha <- uniroot(   function(alpha) {     calibrated <- true_risks(list(treatment = 1, illness = alpha))     calibrated["illness"] - placebo_risks["illness"]   },   interval = c(1, 5),   tol = 0.01 )$root calibrated_risks <- true_risks(list(treatment = 1, illness = true_alpha))  check <- contrasts$estimate[, c("contrast", "estimate", "lower", "upper")] check$truth <- c(   treatment_risks["death"] - placebo_risks["death"],   treatment_risks["death"] - calibrated_risks["death"],   calibrated_risks["death"] - placebo_risks["death"] ) check #>      contrast    estimate      lower         upper    truth #>        <char>       <num>      <num>         <num>    <num> #> 1:      total -0.18273318 -0.3182293 -0.0472370913 -0.13528 #> 2:   mediated -0.06387838 -0.1280762  0.0003194037 -0.05329 #> 3: calibrated -0.11885480 -0.2768993  0.0391897229 -0.08199

title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_estimate() targets initial fit estimate target, risk(death), stochastic intensity intervention: fixed scaling intensity process, scale_intensity(illness = 0.5), one calibrated bring exposure given value, calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate standard error efficient influence curve. intervention_curve() traces target responds exposure grid scalings, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness raises risk death, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package, whose output fit_initial() takes .
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 )  tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), scale_intensity(illness = 0.5)) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) #> #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.2906665 0.03341164 0.2251809 0.3561521 #> #> Initial estimate: 0.2907; no targeting needed, as it already solves the EIC equation

title: Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts — calibrated_contrasts
code: # A trial where treatment lowers the risk of illness, which raises # the risk of death: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = treatment ~ biomarker )  # \donttest{ # How much of the effect of treatment on death goes through its effect on # the risk of illness? The calibrated intervention gives the treated the # risk of illness they would have had under placebo (reference_a = 0): contrasts <- calibrated_contrasts(   treatment_fit = tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), a = 1),   placebo_fit = tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), a = 0),   calibrated_fit = tmle_estimate(     fit,     risk(death),     calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(1), reference_a = 0),     a = 1   ) ) contrasts #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast    estimate         se      lower         upper #>    <char>     <char>       <num>      <num>      <num>         <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.18273318 0.06913193 -0.3182293 -0.0472370913 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.06387838 0.03275458 -0.1280762  0.0003194037 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.11885480 0.08063644 -0.2768993  0.0391897229  # The total effect is the sum of the mediated and calibrated contrasts: sum(contrasts$estimate$estimate[2:3]) - contrasts$estimate$estimate[1] #> [1] 0 # }

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: data data.frame observed event history data long format, one row per event columns id, time event (name process jumped), plus baseline covariates used models. format simevent::simulate_events(). models list hazard model event process: formula death ~ biomarker + illness, naming process left covariates right, hazard_model() also restrict individuals risk . processes can used covariates name, giving number events far. Every event data needs model, including censoring process. tau Positive number. Follow-horizon; target parameters evaluated tau. censoring String. Name censoring process models. treatment_model Optional logistic regression model baseline treatment, two-sided formula treatment ~ biomarker. Required arms given. arms Integer vector baseline treatment values (0/1) prepare interventional hazards clever weights . value can passed tmle_estimate() intervention_curve(). Defaults values, 0:1, treatment_model given. max_count Positive integer. Maximum number jumps tracked per recurrent process state space. depend_time Experimental, may change. Named list one-sided formulas time, making hazards depend time jump. named state variable: process illness jumps , illness.k kth jump recurrent process illness. adds covariate T.<name>, 0 jump formula evaluated time jump , can used (factor) models. example, list(illness = ~ time > 0.5) distinguishes early late jumps. control named list tuning settings: prune_states (FALSE): TRUE, prune states admissible -risk conditions models. use_exponential (FALSE): TRUE, always transform hazard increments dH probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise done increments exceed 1. hal_control named list settings processes fitted fit = "hal", see Details. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() predicting hazards across states. verbose Logical. TRUE, print model fits progress.

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: object class initial_fit, list elements: n: number individuals. tau, treatment_model arms: given (arms default filled ). models: hazard models, list hazard_model()s named process. processes: data.table one row per process columns name, type ("terminal", "recurrent" "one_jump", inferred data), model at_risk (whether process limit at_risk condition). cox_fits: fitted survival::coxph() model process, named process. recurrent process z model fitted indicators (z >= 1) + ... + (z >= max_count). as_sim_model() builds simulation model . also contains internal elements used tmle_estimate(), among tmp_long (expanded data fitted hazards clever weights) depend_matrix (product state space).

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: HAL fits experimental require fit.hal() function available search path. hal_control may contain cut_time (35), cut_one_way (15), cut_tk (3), cut_tk_values (NULL), two_way (NULL), reduce_nk (0.025), sl (list HAL library specifications, built cut_one_way, cut_tk, cut_tk_values two_way default), screen_two_way (FALSE), lambda_cvs, event_dependent_cv (FALSE), npenalize_vars (NULL), v_folds (10), seed (NULL), reduce_seed_dependence (FALSE), penalize_time (FALSE) verbose (FALSE), defaults parentheses. Columns data named process, event counts simevent::simulate_events() adds, ignored: counts recomputed event.

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
code: # Illness-death data: illness is an illness that can occur once, death ends # follow-up, and so does censoring. One row per event: head(illness_death) #>   id      time     event  biomarker treatment #> 1  1 2.8926838 censoring  0.2724785         1 #> 2  2 0.1282264   illness  0.3572619         0 #> 3  2 1.2558891     death  0.3572619         0 #> 4  3 0.6567113     death -0.8616620         0 #> 5  4 0.1752960   illness  0.8083350         1 #> 6  4 0.2409278     death  0.8083350         1  # One hazard model per process. The death hazard depends on whether the # individual has fallen ill, and the illness can occur at most once: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 ) fit #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE  # The process types are inferred from the data, and the hazard models are # kept for reference: fit$processes #>         name     type                                   model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE fit$models$death #> Hazard model: death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness  # With a baseline treatment, a treatment model prepares estimates under # both arms, for `a` in tmle_estimate(): fit_treated <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = treatment ~ biomarker ) fit_treated #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type                                   model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>                                  <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   illness one_jump         illness ~ biomarker + treatment    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal                   censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE #>  #> Treatment model: treatment ~ biomarker, prepared for arms a = 0, 1  # \donttest{ # Data simulated with simevent can be passed as is. Here relapse is # recurrent, and the death hazard grows with the number of relapses so far, # tracked up to max_count: if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {   model <- simevent::sim_model(     biomarker = simevent::sim_covariate(function(N) rnorm(N)),     relapse = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.6, nu = 1),     death = simevent::sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     censoring = simevent::sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     effects = list(       simevent::sim_effect(relapse ~ biomarker, coef = 0.5),       simevent::sim_effect(death ~ relapse, coef = 0.4)     )   )   relapses <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 200, seed = 1)    fit_initial(     relapses,     models = list(       relapse ~ biomarker,       death ~ biomarker + relapse,       censoring ~ biomarker     ),     tau = 2,     max_count = 3   ) } #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 2 #>  #>         name      type                       model at_risk #>       <char>    <char>                      <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   relapse recurrent         relapse ~ biomarker   FALSE #> 2:     death  terminal death ~ biomarker + relapse   FALSE #> 3: censoring  terminal       censoring ~ biomarker   FALSE # }

title: Stochastic intensity interventions — interventions
text: scale_intensity() fixed intensity-scaling intervention: multiplies intensity named process factor alpha, \(\Lambda^z \mapsto \alpha \Lambda^z\). alpha = 1 intervention, alpha < 1 attenuates process alpha > 1 intensifies . calibrate() calibrated intervention: intensity process exposure scaled alpha brings exposure value given toward. target composite parameter, whose standard error accounts alpha estimated. calibration rules : level(theta): exposure equals theta. absolute_change(delta): exposure delta plus value without intervention. relative_change(rho): exposure rho times value without intervention.

title: Stochastic intensity interventions — interventions
code: # Fixed intensity scalings. Halve the intensity of illness, remove illness # altogether, or double it: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5) scale_intensity(illness = 0) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0) scale_intensity(illness = 2) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 2)  # A time-varying scaling: halve the intensity of illness before time 0.5 # only. scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1))  # A scaling that depends on a baseline covariate: halve it only for # individuals with biomarker > 0. scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1))  # A scaling that depends on the number of events so far: halve the # intensity of a recurrent process until its first event only. scale_intensity(relapse = ~ ifelse(relapse == 0, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(relapse = ~ifelse(relapse == 0, 0.5, 1))  # Several processes at once: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5, death = 0.8) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(illness = 0.5, death = 0.8)  # Calibrated interventions, scaling the intensity of illness so that its risk # equals 0.1, falls by 0.05, or falls to 80% of its value without # intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) calibrate(risk(illness), absolute_change(-0.05)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), absolute_change(-0.05)) calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(illness), relative_change(0.8))  # Use them in tmle_estimate(): fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(illness ~ biomarker + treatment, limit = 1),     death ~ biomarker + treatment + illness,     censoring ~ biomarker   ),   tau = 1 ) tmle_estimate(   fit,   risk(death),   scale_intensity(illness = ~ ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) ) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(illness = ~ifelse(biomarker > 0, 0.5, 1)) #>  #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3053054 0.03359683 0.2394568 0.3711539 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.3053; no targeting needed, as it already solves the EIC equation # \donttest{ tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1))) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under calibrate(risk(illness), level(0.1)) #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se     lower     upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:    alpha 0.2176164 0.02987141 0.1590696 0.2761633 #> 2:    theta 0.1000000 0.00000000 0.1000000 0.1000000 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se    lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.2607342 0.03592421 0.190324 0.3311443 0.03559196 #
